text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms, which is why it is often called the "silent killer". Measuring your blood pressure with a cuff is the only way to know if you have it.
When blood pressure becomes dangerously high (typically above 180/120 mm Hg), some people may experience symptoms:

If your blood pressure reading is above 180/120 mm Hg and accompanied by any warning signs of a hypertensive emergency—such as chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a change in vision, or difficulty speaking—call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately.
You can learn more about monitoring your levels through the American Heart Association or review general guidelines via the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
